region: Hector · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Chateau LaFayette Reneau was founded in 1985 by Dick Reno in Hector, on the east shore of Seneca Lake, and its tasting room sits in a carefully restored, century-old barn looking out over the water. The 110-acre estate of stony shale slopes has built its name on vinifera wines, winning New York’s Governor’s Cup three times. Gene Pierce, who also owns Glenora and Knapp, has owned the winery since 2013, with veteran winemaker Tim Miller in the cellar.

Syrah is a bold choice this far north. The grape of the northern Rhône needs warmth and a long season, and on Seneca Lake it relies on the moderating effect of the deep lake, which holds summer heat into autumn. In cooler sites Syrah tends toward pepper, savory and smoked-meat notes rather than jammy fruit, and the winery ages it with oak, which adds a layer of spice to the wine.

The winery’s notes describe black fruit, plum and black cherry with a spicy edge, then the meatiness and black pepper typical of the grape, framed by oak spice. The previous vintage, the 2018 Estate Syrah, was named Best Syrah at the 2023 New York Wine Classic with a 94-point Gold Medal, a sign of how seriously the winery takes this unusual Finger Lakes red.
facts: 110 acres on stony shale, east side of Seneca Lake
